categories.main_business_segments: QXO (formerly SilverSun Technologies) is transitioning to become a tech-forward leader in the building products distribution industry, following a spin-off of its legacy business application, technology, and consulting operations. The legacy business, now SilverSun Holdings, focuses on providing business management software (ERP, HCM, WMS, CRM, BI), managed IT services, cybersecurity, and application hosting to small and medium-sized businesses. QXO itself will serve as a standalone platform for acquisitions and operations in the building products distribution sector.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The legacy business leverages leading ERP platforms (Sage, Acumatica, Sage Intacct), proprietary software integrations, and custom development for ERP enhancements. It employs a dual-shore software development approach, with U.S.-led teams and offshore developers, and offers managed IT services including cybersecurity, disaster recovery, and cloud hosting. The company is a Sage Certified Gold Development Partner, enabling deep customization and integration capabilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Historically, the primary customers have been small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in manufacturing, distribution, and professional services. The company also targets compliance-driven and regulated industries for its cybersecurity offerings. QXO’s future focus will be on customers in the building products distribution industry.
categories.geographic_coverage: The legacy business serves customers nationwide across the United States, with concentrations in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area, Arizona, Connecticut, Southern California, North Carolina, Washington, Oregon, and Illinois. It has expanded its footprint through acquisitions in various regions and maintains a national presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: QXO, post-spin, will operate as a distributor in the building products supply chain, focusing on downstream activities—acquisition and distribution of building products. The legacy business operated as a value-added reseller (VAR) and managed service provider, positioned downstream, delivering software, services, and IT solutions directly to end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: QXO’s strategic focus is on building a tech-forward, acquisition-driven platform in the building products distribution industry. The legacy business emphasized organic growth through recurring revenue, customer retention, and cross-selling, as well as expansion via acquisitions of MSPs, ISVs, and VARs. R&D efforts include ongoing development of ERP enhancements, integrations, and new product extensions, with a focus on cloud-based solutions and cybersecurity.
categories.revenue_model: The legacy business generated revenue through a mix of software product sales, professional consulting services, managed IT services, application hosting, and recurring subscription-based offerings. Many services are billed monthly, increasing monthly recurring revenue (MRR). QXO’s future revenue model will be based on product distribution and potentially value-added services within the building products sector.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The legacy business competed in highly fragmented markets with both large national firms and numerous small, local competitors in ERP software, managed services, and consulting. It positioned itself as one of the largest Sage and Acumatica partners in North America, with unique expertise in both software and hardware. QXO’s future competitors will be other major building products distributors and tech-enabled distribution platforms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2023, the legacy business reported revenues of $54.5 million, up 21% from the prior year, with a net loss of $1.07 million due to deal costs. The company has a history of growth through both organic means and acquisitions. Following a $1 billion equity investment led by Jacobs Private Equity II, QXO will have significant financial resources to pursue large-scale acquisitions and rapid expansion in its new sector.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The legacy business differentiated itself through deep expertise in ERP customization, proprietary software integrations, and the ability to deliver turnkey solutions combining software and hardware. Its value proposition included strong customer retention, responsive support, and the ability to cross-sell a broad suite of advanced technologies. QXO aims to create a differentiated, tech-enabled distribution platform in the building products industry, leveraging scale, technology, and acquisition synergies.
